newsitem.title: USA: China envoy highlghts Taiwan in relations with U.S..
newsitem.headline: China envoy highlghts Taiwan in relations with U.S..

text.p: One day after the death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping, the Chinese ambassador to the United States said Taiwan is the most important issue in relations between the two countries.

At a conference on Thursday commemorating the 25th anniversary of the Shanghai communique -- which also became an occasion for paying tribute to Deng for his role in reforms and opening China to the world -- Ambassador Li Dao Yu said: "Let's not forget that the Taiwan question is the most important and sensitive in our relations."

The Shanghai communique was issued at the conclusion of the meetings between former President Richard Nixon and Chinese Premier Zhou Enlai on Feb. 27, 1972, seven years before the two countries established formal diplomatic ties.
"Taiwan is an inseparable part of China," said Li.
"The Taiwan question involves the national feeling of 1.2 billion Chinese people," he continued. "And this brooks no interference from any foreign country."

Peter Tarnoff, Acting Secretary of State, also speaking at the conference, reiterated the "enduring commitment" of the United States to the one-China policy, which he said "provides the stability for peaceful settlement of the Taiwan question."
But no single question should put the complex relations between the United States and China on hold, Tarnoff said.

Calling the Korean Peninsula "the most dangerous flashpoint," Tarnoff said it was essential to work with China on regional security. The same cooperation is needed to stop the spread of nuclear proliferation, he added.
With thousands of U.S. citizens residing in Hong Kong and U.S. firms doing business there, the United States will have a significant stake in Hong Kong's future, Tarnoff said.
Tarnoff also said the U.S. trade deficit with China is a "major concern" and China must further open its market before gaining access to the World Trade Organisation.

Cyrus Vance, who served as secretary of state from 1977-80, echoed Tarnoff's view on comprehensive engagement, told the conference that the U.S-China relations should not hinge on one issue and urged both sides to "seek ways to share concerns."
Henry Kissinger, Secretary of State from 1973-1977, said Deng's retirement from politics three years ago allowed the Chinese leaders to prepare for the transfer of power.
"I believe the transition will be smooth," he said, adding, "The opaquness of the political system is carefully preserved."
